spans.text: All functional images were initially realigned to adjust for motion-related artifacts. Volume-based realignment was performed by co-registering images using rigid-body transformation to minimize the squared differences between volumes. The realigned images were then spatially normalized with the Montreal Neurologic Institute (MNI) template based on the affine and nonlinear registration of co-registered T1-weighted anatomic images (normalization procedure of SPM). They were resampled into 3 × 3 × 3 mm voxels with sinc interpolation. Images were spatially smoothed using a Gaussian kernel of 6 × 6 × 6 mm full width at half-maximum.

The activations in the left inferior temporal gyrus, the bilateral postcentral gyrus, and the bilateral rolandic operculum were significantly greater in the visuotactile condition than those in the visuomotor condition.
In contrast, the left central sulcus was more activated in the visuomotor condition than in the visuotactile condition.
We observed greater activations in the left hippocampus and the right thalamus in the synchronous condition than those in the asynchronous condition.
